general: One does not simply walk into Mordor — one also needs to pack adequate supplies, arrange a will, and leave a very apologetic note for one's relatives.
The Fellowship spent three days arguing about which route to take, which was not unusual for a group of nine that included three different opinions per person.
Gandalf's arrival at Bilbo's party was precisely timed, which is more than can be said for his arrival at most meetings of actual strategic importance.
The ring of power turned out to be entirely plain in appearance, which was either proof of great evil or very poor branding.
Second breakfast is not a luxury in the Shire — it is a moral and philosophical necessity recognized by all reasonable people.
Legolas counted his kills throughout the battle while Gimli accused him of creative accounting, which is not something most battles feature prominently.
The eagles showed up at the last moment, as eagles do, leaving everyone to wonder why they couldn't have offered a lift several hundred miles earlier.
Saruman, for all his great power and centuries of learning, ultimately lost his tower to a group of very angry trees, which is a cautionary tale.
Pippin dropped a stone into a well in Moria and in doing so demonstrated that hobbits have an unusual talent for precisely wrong actions at precisely wrong moments.
Gollum's internal debate about the Ring was the most dramatic monologue in Middle-earth, performed entirely by one person for an audience of one person.
The Balrog of Moria had terrorized Khazad-dûm for centuries and was ultimately undone by a wizard who had been technically dead for three days.
Aragorn spent most of his life hiding in the wilderness as a ranger and then appeared at Rivendell looking exactly like someone who had been hiding in the wilderness.
Merry and Pippin's primary strategic contributions to the War of the Ring involved eating well, growing tall, and starting a revolution among the trees.
The Ringwraiths were among the most feared beings in Middle-earth and were consistently defeated by fire, water, and a small woman saying a memorable sentence.
Frodo has now left the Shire twice and returned once, which puts him significantly ahead of most hobbits on the adventuring-to-returning ratio.
gandalf: You shall not pass! — though I admit I said it with somewhat more confidence than I felt at the time, which is the essence of good leadership.
I am a wizard; I make things look more impressive than they are, which is, now that I think about it, most of what wizardry consists of.
Fly, you fools! — admittedly not my most instructive farewell, but I was falling at the time, which limits one's capacity for detailed instruction.
Saruman once called me a fool of a Took, but that was Pippin; either way, the sentiment was misplaced — Tooks are surprisingly resilient.
I spent twenty years watching Bilbo before deciding it was time to send him on an adventure; I consider this commendable patience.
The problem with being a wizard is that everyone expects fireworks when what is really needed is a very precise and boring conversation.
sam: Potatoes! Boil 'em, mash 'em, stick 'em in a stew — Gollum, I ask you, what is wrong with potatoes? This is not a difficult concept.
I said I'd go with Mr. Frodo to the ends of the earth, and it turns out the ends of the earth are significantly less pleasant than the name implies.
The Gaffer always said don't get mixed up with wizards; I should have listened, but then again he also said mushrooms were overrated, so his judgment is questionable.
I didn't want to see mountains or elves or dragon-country or thunderstorms on the way to the destination — and I got all of it, plus orcs.
legolas: A red sun rises — blood has been spilled this night. Gimli told me this was needlessly dramatic, which I found rich coming from someone who screams when counting.
My eyes can see twenty miles in clear conditions; this has never helped me find anything when I actually needed to find it.
gimli: Nobody tosses a dwarf — but if they offer to carry one politely and explain their reasons, we can sometimes be persuaded.
I never thought I would die fighting side by side with an elf, and yet I am almost getting used to the company, which alarms me somewhat.
The mines of Moria were magnificent once, and they will be magnificent again, once we deal with the Balrog and replace the ventilation.
frodo: I feel thin, sort of stretched, like butter scraped over too much bread — which is a metaphor, not a recipe, though I could go for some butter right now.
I volunteered to take the Ring because no one else would, which seemed noble at the time; I have since developed a more nuanced view of volunteering.
Gollum has been both my worst companion and my best guide, which is the kind of paradox that makes a very long journey feel even longer.
